response.sql: WITH site_counts AS (SELECT s.healtheval, COUNT(DISTINCT c.zoneref) AS site_count FROM scanconservation c JOIN sites s ON s.zoneregistry = c.zoneref GROUP BY s.healtheval), shares AS (SELECT healtheval, site_count, site_count * 1.0 / SUM(site_count) OVER () AS share FROM site_counts), ranked AS (SELECT healtheval, site_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT AVG(site_count) AS avg_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM ranked WHERE share > avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: The three summary averages (count, share, and excess over average share) are computed over only the statuses whose share is above the average share. The average share threshold itself is computed over all statuses, including the missing-status group.
The inner join on scanconservation.zoneref = sites.zoneregistry is what drops records with no matching site.
GROUP BY healtheval puts all NULL statuses into one group, which is treated as its own status.

Standard SQL with window functions and CTEs is used. The schema's type notation looks PostgreSQL-style, but no dialect was specified. No rounding is applied, and the share is computed with 1.0 to avoid integer division.

alternatives.interpretation: Average count is taken over all statuses, not just the above-average ones. Only the average share and the average excess are restricted to the above-average statuses.
alternatives.sql: WITH site_counts AS (SELECT s.healtheval, COUNT(DISTINCT c.zoneref) AS site_count FROM scanconservation c JOIN sites s ON s.zoneregistry = c.zoneref GROUP BY s.healtheval), shares AS (SELECT healtheval, site_count, site_count * 1.0 / SUM(site_count) OVER () AS share FROM site_counts), ranked AS (SELECT healtheval, site_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT (SELECT AVG(site_count) FROM ranked) AS avg_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM ranked WHERE share > avg_share;
